title: GAN
description: Generative model employing adversarial zero-sum training between generator and discriminator.
name: GAN
summary: GANs (Generative Adversarial Networks) train two neural networks simultaneously: a Generator that creates realistic samples and a Discriminator that attempts to distinguish real data from generated samples, optimizing a minimax objective.
use_when: Generating high-fidelity synthetic images, performing style transfers, or super-resolution tasks.
avoid_when: Working with discrete sequence text generation, where autoregressive models perform better.
pros: Generates extremely sharp, high-fidelity synthetic image files.
Can learn complex, high-dimensional probability distributions without explicit modeling.
Wide variety of specialized architectures (e.g. CycleGAN, Pix2Pix).
cons: Highly unstable to train, prone to mode collapse or vanishing gradients.
Extremely sensitive to balancing generator and discriminator learning rates.
No direct way to calculate sample likelihood or reconstruct latent variables.

key_hyperparams.name: latent_dim
key_hyperparams.note: Dimensionality of the input noise vector for the generator.

quick_start:
import torch.nn as nn
import torch

# Minimal generator architecture
generator = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(10, 64), nn.ReLU(), nn.Linear(64, 784), nn.Tanh())
noise = torch.randn((1, 10))
sample = generator(noise)
